q: Are alloy steel bars, sections and wire under CN 7224 to 7229 covered by CBAM?
title: CBAM CN 7224 to 7229: alloy steel
short: Yes. Other alloy steel, from semi-finished (7224) through flat products (7225, 7226), bars and rods (7227, 7228) to wire (7229), is covered under the Chapter 72 line. Direct emissions only. Forging and auto-component suppliers ship a lot of 7228.
audience: Alloy and special steel makers supplying EU forging and auto buyers

p: Yes. Every heading from 7224 to 7229 sits inside Chapter 72. Grain-oriented electrical steel falls under 7225 and 7226 and is also covered. Forged parts made from these bars usually leave Chapter 72, so check the final code.

ul: Pig iron, DRI and agglomerated ore, if your route uses them.
Ferro-manganese, ferro-chrome and ferro-nickel. Other alloying additions such as ferro-molybdenum or ferro-vanadium are not covered precursors.

p: The Commission sets default values by CN code and country of origin in the annex to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2621, with a mark-up that rises over the first years. We do not quote the figure here. Open the annex, find your code and India, and treat it as the number your buyer pays on if you send nothing usable.

sections.h: What to send your EU importer
ul: Direct embedded emissions per tonne of alloy steel product, in tonnes of CO2, for the period the importer asks about.
The production route and the installation's name, location and, if registered, its CBAM registry ID.
Each precursor's embedded emissions and quantity per tonne, and who made it if you bought it.
Whether a verifier accredited for CBAM has checked the figure. The importer can only use actual values that are verified.

p: Treating every ferro-alloy as a precursor. Only 7202 1 (FeMn), 7202 4 (FeCr) and 7202 6 (FeNi) are covered. Others such as SiMn, FeSi and FeMo add no precursor emissions, so you do not need supplier figures for them.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and purchase invoices into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for. It does not file CBAM declarations or verify emissions.
